To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
HMTD undergoes gas phase reactions with amines and methanol to form new products that are detectable by mass spectrometry.
the detection of HMTD in mass spectrometry is limited by the formation of a stable adduct of HMTD to the solvent in the APCI or ESI source.
the gas-phase reaction of HMTD with primary and secondary amins in the APCI ion source conserves hydrogen peroxide and that TMDD is the product.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a method for detecting trace amounts of HMTD and the characterization of the products formed in the mass spectrometer.
improving the limits of detection (LOD) for HMTD.
the development of a method that can be used to improve detection of HMTD.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
HMTD detection is best accomplished with the APCI source and the [HMTD + MeOH2–H 2O2]+ product. [1]
the addition of aminies to the HMTD solution does not improve detection of HMTD in mass spectrometry.
the addition of aminies to the post-column HMTD environment does not improve the detection of the analyte, but the addition of a primary amine to the APCI source does improve HMTD sensitivity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have improved HMTD detection in the APCI mode by 2.5 orders of magnitude.
HMTD detection in ESI-MS is improved when methanol is present in the sample and the APCI source is used to generate the TMDDD product in the presence of amines.

HMTD detection in the ESI source is limited by the amount of methoxy HMTD formed in the APCI ion source, and the detection of HMTD in the APCI is limited by the formation of TMDDD in the ion source. [1]
The main takeaway from our work is that
the HMTD reaction in the APCI ion source with primary and secondary amins is a viable method to lower the detection of HMTD in mass spectrometry.
HMTD is not a stable compound in the gas phase.
the detection of HMTD can be significantly improved by generating the product [HMTD + MeOH2–H20]+. [1]
